metaDescription: Hold severed minerals under Dove Valley office parks in Arapahoe County? We evaluate title and make a direct, no-obligation offer.
heroLead: Dove Valley is corporate office park today, but the mineral estate under it was almost always severed generations before the first building went up.
intro: It surprises a lot of owners to learn they still hold mineral rights under developed commercial ground in Arapahoe County. Surface development does not extinguish a mineral estate; it just makes drilling on that specific tract unlikely, since no operator wants to put a rig pad in the middle of an office campus.

That does not make the interest worthless. It may still be part of a larger horizontal drilling unit that reaches under Dove Valley from a pad drilled somewhere else nearby, which is how most DJ Basin development actually reaches suburban ground now.

sections.heading: How minerals under a business park get produced
paragraphs: Horizontal wells drilled from a pad a mile or more away can extend laterals underneath developed surface like Dove Valley without ever disturbing it. If your tract is inside a pooled unit, you can be receiving royalty income even though there is no visible well anywhere near your property.

sections.heading: Confirming your interest actually exists
paragraphs: The first step for ground like this is confirming through Arapahoe County records whether your mineral interest was ever severed, and if so, whether it sits inside an active unit. Some owners in this area hold minerals with no unit designation at all, which changes the offer to reflect undeveloped rather than producing acreage.

sections.heading: Pricing suburban severed minerals
paragraphs: If you are inside a unit and receiving royalty checks, we price off that revenue and its decline trend. If you are not currently in a unit, we price against comparable undeveloped mineral sales nearby, which run lower since there is no production to underwrite against.

sections.heading: Timing a sale against a unit's status
paragraphs: If your Dove Valley tract is not yet part of a producing unit, timing is largely out of your hands, since it depends on when, or whether, an operator drills a pad that reaches under this ground. Owners who would rather have a known number now than wait on that uncertainty are the ones who typically call us first.

faqs.question: I did not know I owned minerals under my office building. How do I check?
faqs.answer: We can search Arapahoe County deed and unit records against your legal description to confirm whether a severance occurred and whether it is in an active unit.

faqs.question: Can a well ever be drilled directly under Dove Valley?
faqs.answer: Unlikely given the developed surface, but horizontal laterals from nearby pads can reach the mineral estate without any surface disturbance here.

faqs.question: If I am not receiving royalties, is my interest worth anything?
faqs.answer: It can still have value based on the possibility of future unitization, priced conservatively against comparable undeveloped sales.

faqs.question: What if no well ever reaches under my Dove Valley tract?
faqs.answer: That is a real possibility on developed suburban ground far from any surface pad. We price unleased interests conservatively with that risk already factored in.
